Artane-Whitehall (Artane, Whitehall, Beaumont, Killester) — Dublin, Ireland

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

Press coverage of the Artane-Whitehall LEA (Artane, Whitehall, Beaumont, Killester) shows a handful of serious but isolated incidents rather than an ongoing crime pattern. The most significant was a fatal one-punch assault on Larkhill Road, Whitehall, Dublin 9, in the early hours of 30 July 2023: a man was struck outside a taxi during a row over the car door and died two days later; a suspect was charged with manslaughter, with the case sent forward for trial through late 2024. Separately, an armed carjacking occurred in Artane on 4 May 2022, in which a motorist was threatened at gunpoint ('give me the car or I will blow your head off') and with a knife; one participant, a juvenile at the time, was convicted in February 2026, with sentencing pending. More recently, gardai confirmed a fatal incident at a residential address on Brookwood Heights, Artane, in the early hours of 16 May 2026, in which a man in his 30s died and a man in his 60s was arrested and detained — details suggest a contained, likely domestic-type incident rather than street crime, with the Garda investigation still active at time of writing. No evidence was found of the area being a recognised 'no-go' zone, of organised gang turf conflict, or of frequent daytime muggings, assaults on tourists, or repeated public-order disorder specific to Artane, Whitehall, Beaumont or Killester (unlike nearby Coolock, which saw distinct asylum-accommodation protest violence in mid-2024, but which falls outside this LEA). Daytime searches turned up no particular safety concerns — shops, parks, DART stations and residential streets show no reported pattern of incidents. Night-time carries modestly more caution given the documented fatal assault, carjacking and fatal domestic incident, all clustered around late-night/early-morning hours, though these read as isolated serious events years apart rather than a chronic hotspot. Sources checked: The Irish Times (irishtimes.com); TheJournal.ie (thejournal.ie); Garda.ie / Crimecall (garda.ie); BreakingNews.ie (breakingnews.ie); Kildare Nationalist (kildare-nationalist.ie); Echo Live (echolive.ie); Donegal Daily (donegaldaily.com).
